newsitem.title: JAPAN: KCE SAYS GRAIN FUTURES CONTRACT MAY BE DELAYED.
newsitem.headline: KCE SAYS GRAIN FUTURES CONTRACT MAY BE DELAYED.

text.p: The Kansai Commodity Exchange (KCE) said on Tuesday its plan to list a grain index futures contract may be delayed until early next year, as the Chicago Board of Trade has yet to give approval for use of its prices.
The KCE said last month it would launch the grain index contract, which would be calculated using some CBOT grain market prices including corn, soybean and soymeal, by the end of the year.
The KCE, under the Agriculture Ministry's orders, recently asked CBOT for approval to use its grain market prices for the index futures.

"We've been in contact with CBOT since last month, but they're still hesitating about giving their approval," said Yoshinaga Terada, general manager at KCE's planning department. "We may be forced to delay the listing until early next year, if we can't get their approval quickly."
Terada said he had been told that some CBOT members were reluctant to approve the index because of the possible impact KCE's new grain contract would have on the CBOT market.
"I can't tell when CBOT will give us official approval at this stage," KCE's Terada said.
